principles: Local development remains the default usable path.
Readiness output should be explicit, actionable, and non-authoritative.
Authority server mode is opt-in and receipt-backed.
Docs must prevent users from mistaking status diagnostics for gate evidence.
drivers: Need protect no-server users from accidental enforce blockers.
Need prepare users for later authority runner setup.

options.name: A: extend authority status/readiness plus docs and smoke tests
pros: Creates a clear UI/API contract for later runner work
cons: Does not implement job claim or receipt-backed evidence submission

options.name: B: immediately enforce authority prerequisites globally
pros: Would strongly signal production authority requirements

chosen: A: extend authority status/readiness plus docs and smoke tests
rationale: The user needs both future enforce readiness and current local usability, so status/readiness plus docs gives a safe default without turning paid/server authority into a global requirement.

preMortem.trigger: Status lists missing server URL as an error instead of readiness warning
preMortem.consequence: Local users think Koala cannot run without paid authority
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke asserts off mode has localWorkflowUsable true and productionDone false.

preMortem.trigger: Status shows receiptVerified true or productionDone true without a receipt
preMortem.mitigation: Adversarial smoke asserts no status path can claim receipt-backed authority.

preMortem.scenario: Docs imply local JSON can replace server receipts
preMortem.trigger: Guide describes local/off as equivalent to enforce
preMortem.consequence: Users bypass authority server for production gate
preMortem.mitigation: Docs explicitly state local/off is usable but non-authoritative for production anti-forgery.
